why: One configuration source. The audit (F03) found compiler/targets/tnca-sim-v0.1.json describing a four-tile system with capabilities.sfu=true while rtl/tile/tnca_tile.v elaborated its core with .HAS_SFU(0). A compiler reading that target would emit an SFU instruction the machine raises ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION on. The target must describe the *elaborated instance*, not some module's default, and the only way to keep that true is for the parameters, the target JSON, the capability expectations and the test command to come from one place.

core-sim.description: One core, two Role Contexts. What tb/core/tb_tnca_core.v elaborates, and what every single-core compiler test targets.

platform_binding.what: the testbench that reads this profile's capabilities back out of the hardware

core-4r.description: One core, four Role Contexts, half the logical vector registers each so the physical file is the same size. compiler_overview.md sec 15 C4's P+M0+M1+E profile.

platform_binding.what: the testbench that reads this profile's capabilities back out of the hardware

system-2x2.description: Four tiles in a 2x2 mesh, two Role Contexts per core, four NUCA slices, DRAM behind them. What tb/top/tb_tnca_top.v elaborates.
system-2x2.note: HAS_SFU is 0 here and that is the correct profile, not a defect to be papered over. The contract is explicit: the system's SFU stays off rather than being switched on to remove the inconsistency. What was wrong was the target claiming otherwise.

platform_binding.what: the testbench that reads this profile's capabilities back out of the hardware

core-vrf-sync-v1.description: The same single core with the banked, synchronous, finite-port vector register file. Architecturally identical to core-sim -- same ISA, same register capacity, same two role contexts -- so a difference in a result is a difference in implementation. R3 v2's candidate.

platform_binding.what: the testbench that reads this profile's capabilities back out of the hardware

core-vrf-sync-v2.description: core-vrf-sync-v1 with the R39 hardware switches: VRF_BYPASS (a source being written back is read through the bank's write-first path), FE_NOBUBBLE (a stall costs no second fetch slot) and VRF_PREFETCH (the instruction in D reads its vector sources a cycle early). Same ISA, registers, role contexts and capabilities as v1 -- only the timing differs, so v1 artifacts run here and a difference in a result is a defect. The R39 board image.

platform_binding.what: the testbench that reads this profile's capabilities back out of the hardware

core-vrf-sync-v3.description: core-vrf-sync-v2 with the R39-05/08/10 switches: RCTX_SWITCH (an instruction held in R by a register hazard gives way to another Role Context's, which refetches it once a writeback could have cleared the hazard), LSU_INFLIGHT=2 (two load/store units behind the port, so a load starts while the one ahead waits for memory) and FPU_OVERLAP (ordinary vector FP alongside an SFU pass); and RSLICE, the rctx_slice capability (a launch can give each context its own slice of the accumulators, barriers, descriptors and windows). Same ISA and registers as v1 and v2, whose artifacts run here unchanged. Simulation only until a board image is built with it.

platform_binding.what: the testbench that reads this profile's capabilities back out of the hardware

core-vrf-sync-v4.description: core-vrf-sync-v3 with four Role Contexts instead of two, each keeping its 64 logical vector registers, so the banked file holds 256 (16 KiB) -- the four-context core of the original design (R39-05). A kernel compiled for it runs a grid row on all four (rctx_spmd), each in its own quarter of the per-core resources; v1-v3 artifacts start at most two contexts and run unchanged. Simulation only until a board image is built with it.

platform_binding.what: the testbench that reads this profile's capabilities back out of the hardware

core-vrf-sync-v5.description: core-vrf-sync-v4 with the transfer engine's transposed write (HAS_TENSOR_XPOSE, R38 S1-07) and Role Context pairs (RPAIR): a launch can make contexts 2k and 2k+1 one program's producer and consumer, sharing that program's vector registers and its slice of the per-core resources (R39-12, Mode A). A GEMM's B operand, W transposed, arrives by one transposed transfer instead of sixteen gathers and a repack. Two timing switches on top: the matrix unit reads an MMA's A fragment into a buffer before its sweep (MTX_ABUF; an FP16 K16 command 551 -> 311 cycles), and a context waiting for the matrix unit or the transfer engine gives way to another (RCTX_SWITCH=2). v1-v4 artifacts run unchanged.

platform_binding.what: the testbench that reads this profile's capabilities back out of the hardware

core-vrf-sync-v5-x8.description: core-vrf-sync-v5 with the transfer engine's transposed write extended to 1-byte elements (HAS_TENSOR_XPOSE=2, R41 Stage 2 X8; capability tensor_transpose_8bit): an FP8 MMA B operand read from a K-contiguous weight (torch._scaled_mm's column-major B, a linear layer's W.t()) arrives by one transposed transfer instead of a gather per K row. Everything else is core-vrf-sync-v5, so v1-v5 artifacts run unchanged.

platform_binding.what: the testbench that reads this profile's capabilities back out of the hardware

core-xpose-v1.description: core-sim with the transfer engine's transposed write (ISA sec 9E mod[5]) elaborated: HAS_TENSOR_XPOSE=1 and capability tensor_transpose. Otherwise identical to core-sim, so a difference in a result is the feature. R38 S1-07's first three-layer change.

platform_binding.what: the testbench that reads this profile's capabilities back out of the hardware

core-vrf-sync-v5-x8-g2.description: core-vrf-sync-v5-x8 resized for R41 G2 (evidence/r41/hbm_bw/RESOURCES.md; the author's decisions of 2026-10-28): two Role Contexts instead of four (128 physical vector registers), eight mbarriers instead of 32 and 38-bit barrier epochs instead of 48. The accumulator file keeps its 16 slots. Every instruction, format and capability of v5-x8 is unchanged; artifacts compiled for four contexts or 32 barriers do not run here.

supported_topologies.note: Nothing else is supported. rtl/noc/tnca_core_ni.v computes a 2-bit home and rtl/tnca_top.v fixes N_W=2, so raising NX/NY does not produce a correct 16-slice home or a wide enough source tag (audit F05). An unsupported topology must fail at configuration time rather than elaborate into a machine that misroutes.

bench_args_note: Every Role Context the profile defines is launched. NUM_ROLES reports the count this LAUNCH activated (ISA sec 5.1), not the core's architectural maximum, so a capability read-back that started one context would disagree with a target describing two -- and would be right to. A profile's capabilities are the capabilities of the whole profile.
platform_binding_note: Phase 3.6 section 3.1 separates a compile target from a platform binding: a target describes the ISA, the ABI, the capabilities and the resources, and 'cannot be equated with a particular simulator executable or a particular board'. The bench below is a VERIFICATION binding -- which testbench exercises this profile's capabilities on this host -- and it is deliberately not copied into the generated target the compiler reads. The DEVICE binding lives in python/tnca/device.py, which is the one the runtime uses.
